chose: bundle project extensions into an initialization prelude that assigns registration objects before the ordinary prebuilt client mounts
over: build one replacement client bundle per project
load extension modules at browser runtime
because: the frozen contract keeps zero-extension generation on the prebuilt client, requires offline pages, and requires project JSX to share the client's React runtime

chose: treat extension modules as browser presentation code: bundle without host execution and validate registration semantics in the browser registry
over: import project modules into the Node CLI to validate their default exports
because: host execution would run project side effects during capture, while bundling catches missing/syntax/import failures and the registry can validate the actual browser values before rendering

chose: anchor esbuild metafile paths to the project root and derive reported inputs only from absolute real module inputs
over: reinterpret arbitrary cwd-relative metafile keys after the build
because: absWorkingDir makes esbuild's input address space deterministic across CLI launch directories and explicit synthetic-entry filtering prevents a nonexistent watch target
